question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & 8 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-4y=6 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-4y=6.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=6+4y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=6+4y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6+4y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
